models.name: hrm_time_track_guests
models.description:
Pending invitations for unregistered email addresses awaiting organization membership.

Guests represent unregistered email addresses that have received organization invitations but have not yet created accounts. Each guest invitation contains the invited email address, the organization they were invited to join, and the role they will be assigned upon acceptance. Guests have no system permissions until they complete account registration.

When a guest creates an account using the invited email address, they are automatically added to the organization with their assigned role. The invitation is consumed during account creation and cannot be reused.

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: Primary Key.

foreignFields.name: hrm_time_track_organization_id
foreignFields.description:
Organization that sent the invitation.

This foreign key links the guest invitation to the organization that created it. When the guest accepts the invitation by creating an account, they will be added as a member of this organization.

foreignFields.name: hrm_time_track_role_id
foreignFields.description:
Role that will be assigned when the guest accepts the invitation.

This foreign key references the role definition that will be granted to the user when they create an account and accept the invitation. The role determines the member's permissions within the organization.

plainFields.name: email
plainFields.description:
Email address of the invited guest.

This is the email address that was invited to join the organization. When the guest creates an account using this email address, they will be automatically added to the organization. The email must be unique across all pending invitations.

plainFields.name: status
plainFields.description:
Current status of the invitation.

Valid values are 'pending' for active invitations awaiting acceptance, 'accepted' for invitations that have been consumed during account creation, and 'expired' for invitations that have passed their expiration date.

plainFields.name: expires_at
plainFields.description:
Expiration timestamp for the invitation.

Invitations that have not been accepted by this timestamp are automatically marked as expired. This ensures that old invitations do not remain valid indefinitely.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the invitation was created.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the invitation was last updated.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the invitation was soft deleted.

models.name: hrm_time_track_guest_sessions
models.description:
Temporary session tokens for guest invitation acceptance flow.

This table stores session tokens that allow unregistered guests to complete their organization invitation acceptance process. Each session is tied to a specific guest invitation and provides temporary authenticated access for the invitation acceptance workflow.

Sessions are created when a guest receives an invitation link and expire after a configured time period or upon invitation acceptance/rejection.

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: Primary Key. Unique identifier for each guest session token.

foreignFields.name: hrm_time_track_guest_id
foreignFields.description:
Foreign key to the guest invitation record.

Establishes the relationship between this session token and the pending invitation it belongs to. Each session is associated with exactly one guest invitation, and a single guest may have multiple sessions over time.

plainFields.name: ip
plainFields.description:
Client IP address from which the session was created.

Records the network address of the guest's device for security auditing and session validation purposes.

plainFields.name: href
plainFields.description:
Current page URL when the session was created or last accessed.

Tracks the invitation acceptance page URL for session context and navigation state.

plainFields.name: referrer
plainFields.description:
Referrer URL that led to the invitation acceptance page.

Records the source URL (e.g., email invitation link) for tracking invitation delivery channels.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description:
Timestamp when the guest session was created.

Records the exact time the session token was issued to the guest for invitation acceptance.

plainFields.name: expired_at
plainFields.description:
Timestamp when the guest session expires.

Defines the session validity period for security. Sessions are automatically invalidated after this time to prevent unauthorized access to invitation links.

models.name: hrm_time_track_members
models.description: Registered user accounts with email/password authentication supporting multi-organization membership. Each member account serves as the primary identity for authentication across the platform.

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: Primary key for unique member account identification.

plainFields.name: email
plainFields.description:
Unique email address used for authentication and account identification.

This field serves as the primary identifier for login and must be unique across all members. It is case-sensitive and should be stored in lowercase for consistency.

plainFields.name: password_hash
plainFields.description:
Server-side password hash for authentication verification.

Stores the cryptographic hash of the user's password. Never store plain text passwords. The hash is verified during login attempts.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description:
Timestamp when the member account was first created.

This field is set automatically upon account creation and is never updated. It serves as the official account creation timestamp for auditing purposes.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description:
Timestamp when the member account was last updated.

This field is updated on any modification to account settings or security credentials.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description:
Timestamp when the account was marked as deleted (soft delete).

When set, the account is logically deleted but data is preserved for audit purposes. A NULL value indicates an active account.

models.name: hrm_time_track_member_sessions
models.description:
JWT session tokens for member authentication with organization context scoping.

This table maintains authenticated sessions for hrm_time_track_members actors. Each session is associated with a specific organization context, ensuring multi-tenant data isolation. Sessions track client information (IP, href, referrer) for security auditing and support token expiration for access control.

Sessions are created during login and remain active until expiration or logout. Members can switch organization contexts without creating new sessions, but all data access is scoped to the currently selected organization.

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: Primary Key for session record.

foreignFields.name: hrm_time_track_member_id
foreignFields.description:
References the authenticated member account.

Each session belongs to exactly one hrm_time_track_member. This foreign key establishes the authentication relationship between the session and the member's global identity.

foreignFields.name: hrm_time_track_organization_id
foreignFields.description:
References the organization context for this session.

Per section [13] Session Management, each session is associated with a specific organization context. This ensures multi-tenant data isolation by scoping all session actions to the selected organization.

plainFields.name: ip
plainFields.description:
Client IP address at session creation time.

Captured for security auditing and anomaly detection. Used to identify suspicious login patterns or unauthorized access attempts.

plainFields.name: href
plainFields.description:
Referring URL that initiated the login request.

Tracks the entry point to the authentication flow for security analysis and user experience tracking.

plainFields.name: referrer
plainFields.description:
HTTP referrer header from the login request.

Additional context about how the user arrived at the login page, used for security auditing.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description:
Timestamp when the session was created during login.

Used to calculate session age and enforce expiration policies.

plainFields.name: expired_at
plainFields.description:
Timestamp when the session expires and becomes invalid.

Set at session creation based on configured session duration. Sessions are automatically invalidated after this time for security.

models.name: hrm_time_track_member_password_resets
models.description:
Password reset tokens with expiration for member account recovery.

This table stores temporary, single-use tokens that allow members to reset their forgotten passwords. Each token is cryptographically generated, linked to a specific member, and has a limited validity period for security.

Tokens are created when a member requests a password reset via the forgot password flow. The token is sent to the member's registered email address. When the member uses the token to set a new password, the token is marked as used and cannot be reused.

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: Primary Key.

foreignFields.name: hrm_time_track_member_id
foreignFields.description:
Reference to the member who requested the password reset.

This foreign key links the password reset token to the specific member account that needs recovery. Only the member associated with this token can use it to reset their password.

plainFields.name: token
plainFields.description:
Cryptographically secure token for password reset authentication.

This field contains a unique, random string that serves as proof of authorization for the password reset operation. The token is sent to the member's email and must be provided when setting a new password. Each token is single-use only.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the password reset token was generated.

plainFields.name: expired_at
plainFields.description:
Timestamp when the password reset token expires and becomes invalid.

Tokens have a limited validity period (typically 1 hour) for security. After this timestamp, the token cannot be used to reset the password, and the member must request a new reset token.

plainFields.name: used_at
plainFields.description:
Timestamp when the password reset token was consumed to reset the password.

This field is null until the token is successfully used. Once a token is used to reset a password, this timestamp is set and the token becomes invalid for future use. This prevents replay attacks.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp for soft deletion of the password reset record.

models.name: hrm_time_track_member_email_verifications
models.description:
Email verification tokens for member registration confirmation.

These tokens are generated when a member registers with an unverified email address. The member must click a verification link containing the token to confirm their email ownership before full account activation.

Each token is single-use and expires after a configured time period (typically 24 hours) for security purposes.

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: Primary Key.

foreignFields.name: hrm_time_track_member_id
foreignFields.description:
References the member account awaiting email verification.

Each member can have multiple verification tokens if they request new ones before completing verification. Only the most recent unused token is typically valid.

plainFields.name: token
plainFields.description:
Unique verification token sent to the member's email.

The token is a cryptographically secure random string that the member must provide by clicking the verification link. Once used, the token cannot be reused.

plainFields.name: email
plainFields.description:
Email address being verified.

Stored for display purposes and to confirm the token matches the intended recipient email address.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the verification token was generated and sent to the member's email.

plainFields.name: expired_at
plainFields.description:
Timestamp when the verification token expires.

Tokens typically expire after 24 hours for security. Expired tokens cannot be used for verification.

plainFields.name: used_at
plainFields.description:
Timestamp when the verification token was successfully used to verify the email.

NULL if the token has not been used yet. Once set, the token cannot be reused.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description:
Timestamp when the record was soft deleted.

Used for audit trail while allowing data recovery if needed.

models.name: hrm_time_track_organizations
models.description:
Organization entities serving as the root container for multi-tenant HRM and time tracking data.

Each organization owns employees, departments, roles, and projects within its isolated data boundary. Organizations provide the foundational scope for all business operations and ensure complete data separation between tenants.

Organization settings include identity information (name, description, logo), operational preferences (currency, timezone), and fiscal configuration (fiscal start month) that apply to all entities within the organization.

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: Primary Key for organization entity.

plainFields.name: name
plainFields.description:
Organization display name used for identification across the platform.

The name appears in user interfaces, reports, and communications. It must be unique within the system to avoid confusion when users belong to multiple organizations.

plainFields.name: description
plainFields.description:
Optional detailed description of the organization's purpose and scope.

Provides context for organization members and appears in organizational documentation and profiles.

plainFields.name: logo
plainFields.description:
URL to the organization's logo image for branding purposes.

Displayed in the interface to provide visual identification of the organization context.

plainFields.name: currency
plainFields.description:
ISO currency code (e.g., USD, EUR, KRW) for financial calculations within the organization.

All monetary values including employee pay rates, billable rates, and project budgets use this currency. Changing currency affects all financial data in the organization.

plainFields.name: timezone
plainFields.description:
IANA timezone identifier (e.g., Asia/Seoul, America/New_York) for time-based operations.

All timestamps, work schedules, and time tracking are interpreted relative to this timezone. Affects timesheet week boundaries, timer operations, and reporting.

plainFields.name: fiscal_start_month
plainFields.description:
Month number (1-12) marking the beginning of the organization's fiscal year.

January = 1, February = 2, ..., December = 12. Used for financial reporting, pay period calculations, and timesheet approval cycles aligned with fiscal periods.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the organization was created. Immutable after creation.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the organization settings were last modified.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description:
Timestamp when the organization was soft-deleted. Null indicates active organization.

Soft deletion preserves data for audit purposes while removing the organization from active operations. All child entities become inaccessible when parent organization is deleted.

models.name: hrm_time_track_organization_snapshots
models.description:
Point-in-time snapshots of organization settings for audit trail and history tracking.

These records are immutable once created and preserve the exact state of organization settings at a specific moment in time. They enable complete audit trails for compliance and historical reporting.

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: Primary Key.

foreignFields.name: hrm_time_track_organization_id
foreignFields.description:
Reference to the organization being snapshot.

This foreign key links each snapshot to its parent organization, enabling retrieval of all historical versions of a specific organization's settings.

plainFields.name: name
plainFields.description:
Organization name at the time of snapshot.

Captures the legal or doing-business-as name of the organization as it existed when the snapshot was taken.

plainFields.name: description
plainFields.description:
Organization description at the time of snapshot.

Preserves the business description and mission statement active at snapshot time.

plainFields.name: logo_url
plainFields.description:
Organization logo URL at the time of snapshot.

Stores the logo image URL that was associated with the organization when the snapshot was created.

plainFields.name: currency
plainFields.description:
Base currency code used by the organization at snapshot time.

Captures the three-letter ISO 4217 currency code (e.g., 'USD', 'EUR', 'KRW') that was active when the snapshot was taken.

plainFields.name: timezone
plainFields.description:
Primary timezone for the organization at snapshot time.

Preserves the IANA timezone identifier (e.g., 'Asia/Seoul', 'America/New_York') that was configured when the snapshot was created.

plainFields.name: fiscal_start_month
plainFields.description:
Fiscal year start month (1-12) at snapshot time.

Records which month (1=January, 12=December) marked the beginning of the fiscal year when the snapshot was taken.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description:
Timestamp when this snapshot was created.

Immutably records the exact moment this point-in-time copy was captured for audit purposes.

models.name: hrm_time_track_employees
models.description:
Employee records representing a person's role and status within a specific organization.

Each employee record links a user account to an organization, establishing the person's membership and working relationship within that organizational context. Employee records are organization-scoped, meaning a single user can have independent employee records across multiple organizations.

The employee record defines the person's position, employment type, status, and department assignment within the organization. It serves as the foundation for employment contracts, timesheets, and project assignments.

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: Primary Key for employee records.

foreignFields.name: hrm_time_track_organization_id
foreignFields.description:
Reference to the organization that employs this person.

This foreign key establishes the organizational context for the employee record. All employee data, permissions, and relationships are scoped to this organization. An employee cannot exist without an associated organization.

foreignFields.name: hrm_time_track_member_id
foreignFields.description:
Reference to the user account associated with this employee.

This foreign key links the employee record to the authenticated user account. The member represents the person's global identity across all organizations. Each employee record must have an associated member account.

foreignFields.name: hrm_time_track_department_id
foreignFields.description:
Reference to the department within the organization where this employee works.

This foreign key establishes the employee's departmental assignment. Department assignment is optional and can be updated as organizational structure changes. The department must belong to the same organization as the employee.

foreignFields.name: hrm_time_track_role_id
foreignFields.description:
Reference to the role assigned to this employee within the organization.

This foreign key defines the employee's permissions and access level. Role assignment is optional and can be changed by users with employee management permissions. The role must belong to the same organization as the employee.

plainFields.name: position
plainFields.description:
Job title or position of the employee within the organization.

This field stores the employee's official job title or position name (e.g., 'Senior Developer', 'Marketing Manager'). It is used for display purposes and organizational reporting.

plainFields.name: employment_type
plainFields.description:
Classification of the employee's employment arrangement.

This field categorizes the employment type such as full-time, part-time, contract, or internship. The value must conform to the Employee Employment Type Classification business category.

plainFields.name: status
plainFields.description:
Current employment status of the employee.

This field tracks the employee's active status such as active, on leave, terminated, or pending. The value must conform to the Employee Status Classification business category and affects access and permissions.

plainFields.name: hire_date
plainFields.description:
Date when the employee started working for the organization.

This field records the official start date of employment. It is used for tenure calculations, anniversary tracking, and employment history reporting.

plainFields.name: termination_date
plainFields.description:
Date when the employee's employment ended, if applicable.

This field records the end date for terminated or resigned employees. It is nullable for active employees and is used for employment history and reporting purposes.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this employee record was created in the system.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this employee record was last modified.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this employee record was soft deleted. Null indicates the record is active.

models.name: hrm_time_track_employee_snapshots
models.description:
Point-in-time snapshots of employee records for audit trail and history tracking.

These snapshots capture the complete state of an employee record at specific moments in time, preserving historical data even after employee records are updated or deactivated. Each snapshot contains denormalized copies of all employee fields including organization, user, department, and role assignments.

Snapshots are append-only and immutable once created, providing a reliable audit trail for compliance and historical reporting. They enable reconstruction of employee state at any point in time and support tracking of employment history across status changes, role assignments, and department transfers.

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: Primary Key for employee snapshot record.

foreignFields.name: hrm_time_track_employee_id
foreignFields.description:
Reference to the employee record being snapshot.

This foreign key links the snapshot to its source employee record in hrm_time_track_employees. Multiple snapshots can exist for a single employee, each capturing a different point in time.

foreignFields.name: hrm_time_track_organization_id
foreignFields.description:
Denormalized reference to the organization the employee belongs to.

Stored as a denormalized copy from the employee record to preserve organizational context even if the employee record is later modified or the organization structure changes.

foreignFields.name: hrm_time_track_member_id
foreignFields.description:
Denormalized reference to the user account associated with this employee.

Links the employee snapshot to the hrm_time_track_members user record, preserving the user-employee relationship at the time of snapshot.

foreignFields.name: hrm_time_track_department_id
foreignFields.description:
Denormalized reference to the department assignment at snapshot time.

This field is nullable as department assignment is optional for employees. Captures the department context even if the employee is later reassigned or the department is deleted.

foreignFields.name: hrm_time_track_role_id
foreignFields.description:
Denormalized reference to the role assigned to this employee at snapshot time.

Every active employee must have a role assigned, so this field is not nullable. Preserves the role and permission context even if the role is later changed.

plainFields.name: position_title
plainFields.description:
Denormalized copy of the employee's position or job title at snapshot time.

This optional field captures the employee's specific job role description (e.g., 'Software Engineer', 'Marketing Manager'). Independent of the role assignment which controls system permissions.

plainFields.name: employment_type
plainFields.description:
Denormalized copy of the employee's employment classification at snapshot time.

One of four values: 'full-time', 'part-time', 'contractor', or 'intern'. Used for reporting and compliance purposes, capturing the worker classification at the moment of snapshot.

plainFields.name: status
plainFields.description:
Denormalized copy of the employee's status at snapshot time.

Either 'active' or 'deactivated'. Active employees can log time and submit timesheets, while deactivated employees cannot. This field cannot be null as every employee must have a status.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description:
Timestamp when this snapshot was created.

Records the exact point in time when the employee state was captured. Used for chronological ordering of snapshots and for querying employee state at specific historical moments.

models.name: hrm_time_track_employee_contracts
models.description:
Employment contracts for employees tracking pay terms, working hours, and contract periods.

Each contract defines an employee's compensation and working conditions within an organization. Contracts include start date, optional end date, pay rate, pay period (hourly/daily/weekly/monthly), and working hours per week. Only one contract can be active at any time per employee, with previous contracts automatically ended when new ones are created.

Contract relationships:
- Belongs to {@link hrm_time_track_employees} via foreign key
- Contracts are immutable once ended (historical records)
- Active contracts can be edited (pay rate, pay period, working hours, notes, end date extension) but start date is immutable

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: Primary Key for employee contract records.

foreignFields.name: hrm_time_track_employee_id
foreignFields.description:
References the employee this contract belongs to.

Each employee can have multiple contracts over time, but only one active contract at any given time. When a new contract is created for an employee with an existing active contract, the previous contract is automatically ended.

plainFields.name: start_date
plainFields.description:
Contract start date.

This field is mandatory and immutable once the contract is created. It defines when the employment terms begin.

plainFields.name: end_date
plainFields.description:
Contract end date.

This field is optional. If not set, the contract is considered ongoing until explicitly ended or replaced by a new contract. Can be extended when editing an active contract.

plainFields.name: pay_rate
plainFields.description:
Employee pay rate amount.

This field is mandatory and represents the compensation amount. The actual payment frequency is determined by the pay_period field.

plainFields.name: pay_period
plainFields.description:
Pay period classification.

Allowed values: hourly, daily, weekly, monthly. This field is mandatory and defines how the pay_rate should be interpreted.

plainFields.name: working_hours_per_week
plainFields.description:
Number of working hours per week.

This field is mandatory and defines the expected weekly working hours for the employee under this contract.

plainFields.name: notes
plainFields.description:
Optional notes for the contract.

Can contain additional information or special conditions related to the employment contract.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the contract was created.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the contract was last updated.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description:
Timestamp when the contract was soft deleted.

Used for soft delete functionality to preserve historical contract records.

models.name: hrm_time_track_departments
models.description:
Department organizational units with hierarchical structure within organizations.

Departments categorize employees into organizational units for management and reporting purposes. Each department belongs to exactly one organization and can have a parent department to form a hierarchical structure. Department names must be unique within an organization.

When a department is deleted (soft delete), employees previously assigned to that department have their department field set to null, but the employee records remain intact. Department assignment does not affect an employee's role or permissions.

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: Primary Key.

foreignFields.name: hrm_time_track_organization_id
foreignFields.description:
Foreign key to the organization that owns this department.

Each department belongs to exactly one organization. This establishes the organizational boundary for the department and ensures data isolation between organizations.

foreignFields.name: parent_department_id
foreignFields.description:
Foreign key to the parent department for hierarchical structure.

Optional self-referencing field that enables multi-level department hierarchies. Null value indicates a top-level department with no parent.

plainFields.name: name
plainFields.description:
Department name for identification and display.

Department names must be unique within an organization. This field is used for department selection in employee assignments and for organizational reporting.

plainFields.name: description
plainFields.description: Optional description providing additional context about the department's purpose and responsibilities.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this department was created.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this department was last updated.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this department was soft deleted. Null indicates the department is active.

models.name: hrm_time_track_roles
models.description:
Role definitions within organizations that control user permissions and access levels.

Roles define what actions users can perform within an organization. Each role contains a set of permissions that grant access to specific features like organization management, employee management, project management, time tracking, and reporting. Roles can be either built-in (system-defined with standard permission sets) or custom (user-created with tailored permissions).

Built-in roles provide default permission configurations for common organizational needs, while custom roles allow organizations to create specialized access patterns. Role names must be unique within each organization to prevent confusion and ensure clear permission assignment.

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: Primary Key.

foreignFields.name: hrm_time_track_organization_id
foreignFields.description:
References the organization that owns this role.

Each role belongs to exactly one organization. Roles are organization-scoped and cannot be shared across organizations. This ensures multi-tenancy isolation where each organization manages its own role definitions independently.

plainFields.name: name
plainFields.description:
Human-readable name of the role.

Role names are unique within an organization and are used to identify and display roles in the user interface. Examples include 'Administrator', 'Manager', 'Employee', 'Time Keeper'. The name should be descriptive and distinguishable from other roles in the same organization.

plainFields.name: description
plainFields.description:
Detailed description of the role's purpose and intended use.

The description provides context about what the role is for and what permissions it typically grants. This helps administrators understand when to assign this role to employees. Descriptions can include information about the role's scope, typical use cases, and any special considerations.

plainFields.name: is_builtin
plainFields.description:
Indicates whether this is a built-in system role or a custom user-created role.

Built-in roles are predefined by the system with standard permission sets and cannot be deleted (only soft-deleted). Custom roles are created by organization administrators and can be fully managed including deletion. This distinction helps prevent accidental removal of essential system roles while allowing flexibility for organization-specific needs.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description:
Timestamp when this role was created.

Recorded automatically when the role is first created. Used for audit trail, sorting roles by creation date, and tracking when roles were added to the organization.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description:
Timestamp when this role was last modified.

Updated automatically whenever any field of the role is changed. Used to track role modifications, detect stale data, and support optimistic concurrency control in updates.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description:
Timestamp when this role was soft-deleted.

When set, the role is considered deleted but the record remains in the database for audit purposes. Soft-deleted roles cannot be assigned to new employees but existing assignments remain intact. Built-in roles can only be soft-deleted, never permanently removed.

models.name: hrm_time_track_role_snapshots
models.description:
Point-in-time snapshots of role definitions for audit trail and history tracking.

These snapshots capture the complete state of a role at a specific moment, including name, description, built-in status, and associated permissions. Snapshots are created when roles are created, updated, or deleted to maintain a complete audit history of permission changes within an organization.

Snapshots are append-only and immutable once created. They reference the parent role via foreign key and optionally track which member triggered the snapshot event.

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: Primary Key for role snapshot records.

foreignFields.name: hrm_time_track_role_id
foreignFields.description:
Reference to the role being snapshot.

This foreign key links the snapshot to its parent role in {@link hrm_time_track_roles}. The snapshot captures the state of this role at a specific point in time.

foreignFields.name: created_by_member_id
foreignFields.description:
Reference to the member who triggered this snapshot.

This foreign key identifies which {@link hrm_time_track_members} performed the action that created this snapshot (role creation, update, or deletion). May be null for system-generated snapshots.

plainFields.name: name
plainFields.description:
Role name at the time of snapshot.

This field captures the role's name as it existed when the snapshot was created. Used for audit trail to track name changes over time.

plainFields.name: description
plainFields.description:
Role description at the time of snapshot.

This field captures the role's description as it existed when the snapshot was created. May be null if the role had no description.

plainFields.name: is_builtin
plainFields.description:
Whether this role is a built-in role at the time of snapshot.

Built-in roles (Owner, Manager, Employee) cannot be deleted. This field captures the built-in status at snapshot time for audit purposes.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description:
Timestamp when this snapshot was created.

Records the exact point in time when the role state was captured for audit trail purposes.

models.name: hrm_time_track_role_permissions
models.description:
Junction table linking roles to their granted permissions within organizations.

This table stores the permission assignments for each role. Each role can have multiple permissions, and each permission entry is unique per role. Permissions define what actions are allowed, including organization management, employee management, employee viewing, project management, project viewing, time management, timesheet approval, time viewing all, and report viewing.

The table is append-only with no soft delete since permission changes are handled by removing and re-adding entries rather than marking them deleted.

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: Primary Key for role permission records.

foreignFields.name: hrm_time_track_role_id
foreignFields.description:
Foreign key referencing the role that owns this permission.

Links to {@link hrm_time_track_roles} to establish the relationship between roles and their granted permissions. Each role can have multiple permission entries.

plainFields.name: permission
plainFields.description:
Permission code defining the granted access right.

Valid permission values include: organization_management, employee_management, employee_viewing, project_management, project_viewing, time_management, timesheet_approval, time_viewing_all, and report_viewing. The permission value is validated at the application layer against the allowed permission list.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description:
Timestamp when this permission was granted to the role.

Records the exact time when the permission assignment was created. Used for audit trail and tracking permission changes over time.

models.name: hrm_time_track_role_snapshot_permissions
models.description:
Junction table tracking permissions granted to roles at snapshot time for audit trail.

This table captures the permission set assigned to each role at the moment a role snapshot was created. It enables historical auditing of permission changes by preserving the exact permissions that were granted to a role at specific points in time. Each role snapshot can have multiple permission records, one for each permission granted to that role.

The table maintains referential integrity with {@link hrm_time_track_role_snapshots} and enforces uniqueness to prevent duplicate permissions within the same snapshot.

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: Primary Key for role snapshot permission records.

foreignFields.name: hrm_time_track_role_snapshot_id
foreignFields.description:
Foreign key reference to the role snapshot this permission belongs to.

This field establishes the relationship between a permission record and its parent role snapshot. Each permission record is tied to exactly one role snapshot, enabling the reconstruction of the complete permission set for a role at the time the snapshot was taken.

plainFields.name: permission
plainFields.description:
The permission identifier granted to the role at snapshot time.

This field stores the permission name as a string value. Available permissions include organization_management, employee_management, employee_viewing, project_management, project_viewing, time_management, timesheet_approval, time_viewing_all, and report viewing. The permission value is captured at the time of snapshot creation and remains immutable.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description:
Timestamp recording when this role snapshot permission was created.

This field captures the exact moment when the permission was recorded in the snapshot. Since snapshots are immutable audit records, this timestamp reflects when the snapshot (and its associated permissions) was created and cannot be modified.

models.name: hrm_time_track_projects
models.description:
Main project entity containing project identification, description, and organizational assignment.

Projects represent work containers within organizations that can have tasks, timelogs, and team members assigned. Each project has a lifecycle status (active, archived, or completed) that controls whether new work can be added.

Projects are organization-scoped and cannot be deleted if they have associated timelogs. Project status transitions follow a defined workflow where active projects can be archived or completed, and archived/completed projects can be reactivated.

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: Primary Key for project entity.

foreignFields.name: hrm_time_track_organization_id
foreignFields.description:
Foreign key referencing the organization that owns this project.

Each project belongs to exactly one organization and cannot exist without an organizational parent. The organization provides the multi-tenancy boundary and permission context for project access.

plainFields.name: name
plainFields.description:
Project name for identification and display purposes.

The name uniquely identifies the project within the organization context and is used in user interfaces and reports.

plainFields.name: description
plainFields.description:
Optional detailed description of the project scope and objectives.

Provides additional context about the project's purpose and deliverables.

plainFields.name: color_code
plainFields.description:
Color code for visual display purposes in user interfaces.

Used to visually distinguish projects in dashboards and lists.

plainFields.name: status
plainFields.description:
Current lifecycle status of the project.

Allowed values: 'active' (ongoing, can receive new timelogs), 'archived' (preserved for reference, no new timelogs), 'completed' (finished, no new timelogs). Status controls whether new work can be added to the project.

plainFields.name: budget_hours
plainFields.description:
Optional total estimated hours budget for the project.

Used for tracking and reporting against planned vs actual time investment.

plainFields.name: start_date
plainFields.description:
Optional project start date.

Indicates when the project work began or is scheduled to begin.

plainFields.name: end_date
plainFields.description:
Optional project end date.

Indicates when the project work is scheduled to complete.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the project was created.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the project was last updated.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description:
Timestamp when the project was soft deleted.

Projects can only be deleted if they have no associated timelogs. Soft delete preserves data for audit purposes.

models.name: hrm_time_track_project_members
models.description:
Junction table linking employees to projects with assigned roles and permissions.

This table establishes the assignment relationship between employees and projects, enabling employees to work on specific projects. Each project membership includes a role that defines the employee's authority level within the project context.

Project membership is required for employees to log time, view tasks, and participate in project activities. The membership relationship enforces proper data isolation between projects and authorizes employees to contribute work through timelogs and task assignments.

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: Primary Key for project member records.

foreignFields.name: hrm_time_track_employee_id
foreignFields.description:
Foreign key reference to the employee assigned to the project.

This establishes the employee-project relationship, linking the employee record to their project membership. The employee must be a valid member of the organization that owns the project.

foreignFields.name: hrm_time_track_project_id
foreignFields.description:
Foreign key reference to the project the employee is assigned to.

This links the project membership to the specific project. The employee gains access to project resources, tasks, and time tracking capabilities through this association.

plainFields.name: role
plainFields.description:
The assigned role defining the employee's authority level within the project.

Allowed values are 'member' for standard access to view and contribute to the project, or 'project-lead' for elevated authority to manage tasks within the assigned project. This role-based control ensures appropriate task management permissions are granted.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the project membership was created.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the project membership was last updated.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the project membership was soft deleted. Null indicates active membership.

models.name: hrm_time_track_tasks
models.description:
Individual units of work within projects supporting parent-child hierarchy for task breakdown structures.

Tasks represent discrete pieces of work that belong to projects and can be assigned to employees. The parent-child hierarchy allows breaking down complex work into manageable subtasks with only one level of nesting supported.

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: Primary Key for unique identification of each task.

foreignFields.name: hrm_time_track_project_id
foreignFields.description:
References the project this task belongs to.

Each task must be associated with exactly one project from {@link hrm_time_track_projects}.

foreignFields.name: hrm_time_track_employee_id
foreignFields.description:
References the employee this task is assigned to.

Optional assignment - tasks may exist without an assignee. References {@link hrm_time_track_employees}.

foreignFields.name: parent_task_id
foreignFields.description:
References the parent task for subtask organization.

Only one level of nesting is supported. If set, this task is a subtask of the referenced parent task. Self-referencing foreign key to {@link hrm_time_track_tasks}.

plainFields.name: title
plainFields.description:
Short descriptive name for the task.

Required field that provides a concise identifier for the task.

plainFields.name: description
plainFields.description:
Detailed description of the work to be performed.

Optional field containing comprehensive task details and requirements.

plainFields.name: priority
plainFields.description:
Priority level: low, medium, high, or critical.

Indicates the urgency and importance of completing the task.

plainFields.name: status
plainFields.description:
Current workflow state of the task.

Tracks task progress through its lifecycle stages.

plainFields.name: effort_estimate
plainFields.description:
Estimated effort in hours to complete the task.

Optional field for planning and resource allocation.

plainFields.name: effort_actual
plainFields.description:
Actual effort spent on the task.

Optional field for tracking real time expenditure against estimates.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the task was created.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when the task was last modified.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp for soft delete when task is logically removed.

models.name: hrm_time_track_timelogs
models.description:
Individual time entries recording work performed by employees with date, duration, project, and optional task assignment.

Timelogs represent discrete units of work time logged by employees. Each timelog captures when work was performed, how long it took, which project it relates to, and optionally which specific task. Timelogs are owned by the employee who creates them and cannot be created on behalf of others.

Timelogs form the foundation for timesheet creation and approval workflows. They can be filtered by date range, project, task, and billable status to support reporting and analysis.

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: Primary Key.

foreignFields.name: hrm_time_track_employee_id
foreignFields.description:
Reference to the employee who performed and owns this time entry.

Each timelog is owned by the employee who creates it. Employees can only create timelogs for their own work, ensuring accurate attribution of time to the correct person. This ownership model ensures accountability and accurate time tracking.

foreignFields.name: hrm_time_track_organization_id
foreignFields.description:
Reference to the organization that owns this time entry.

All timelogs are strictly isolated per organization. Employees can only see timelogs within their current organization context. This ensures complete data separation between organizations.

foreignFields.name: hrm_time_track_project_id
foreignFields.description:
Reference to the project this time entry relates to.

Each timelog must be associated with a project. Projects provide the organizational context for time tracking and billing purposes.

foreignFields.name: hrm_time_track_task_id
foreignFields.description:
Optional reference to the specific task this time entry relates to.

Tasks provide more granular tracking within projects. Timelogs can exist without task assignment for general project work.

plainFields.name: date
plainFields.description:
Date when the work was performed.

This field represents the calendar date of the work activity. Timelogs can be filtered by date range to view entries within specific periods.

plainFields.name: duration_seconds
plainFields.description:
Duration of the work in seconds.

Time is stored as an integer number of seconds for precision and ease of calculation. This allows accurate time tracking and reporting.

plainFields.name: billable
plainFields.description:
Whether this time entry is billable to a client.

Billable status separates chargeable work from internal or non-billable activities. Timelogs can be filtered by billable status for billing and reporting purposes.

plainFields.name: notes
plainFields.description:
Optional notes or description of the work performed.

Employees can add contextual information about their time entry to provide details about what was accomplished.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this timelog was created.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description: Timestamp when this timelog was last updated.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description:
Timestamp when this timelog was soft deleted.

Soft delete allows timelogs to be marked as deleted while preserving historical data for audit and reporting purposes.

models.name: hrm_time_track_timesheets
models.description:
Weekly timesheet collections for employee time tracking approval workflow.

Timesheets group timelogs into weekly periods (Monday to Sunday) for submission and approval. Each timesheet belongs to a single employee and represents one week's work. The timesheet follows an approval workflow with four status states: draft, submitted, approved, and rejected.

Timesheets in draft status can be freely modified by employees. Once submitted, timelogs become locked until approval or rejection. Approved timesheets are immutable and serve as the official record. Rejected timesheets return to draft status with a rejection reason for employee review.

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: Primary Key. Unique identifier for each timesheet record.

foreignFields.name: hrm_time_track_employee_id
foreignFields.description:
Foreign key to the employee who owns this timesheet.

Each timesheet belongs to exactly one employee. The employee creates, manages, and submits the timesheet for approval. This relationship enables filtering timesheets by employee and enforcing ownership-based access control.

foreignFields.name: hrm_time_track_member_id
foreignFields.description:
Foreign key to the member who approved this timesheet.

This field is populated only when the timesheet status is 'approved'. The approver must have time:approve permission. This reference enables tracking who approved each timesheet for audit and reporting purposes.

plainFields.name: status
plainFields.description:
Current approval workflow status of the timesheet.

Allowed values: 'draft', 'submitted', 'approved', 'rejected'. New timesheets start as 'draft'. Employees can submit draft timesheets for approval. Users with time:approve permission can approve or reject submitted timesheets. Rejected timesheets return to draft status.

plainFields.name: week_start_date
plainFields.description:
Start date of the timesheet week (Monday).

Timesheets follow a weekly cycle from Monday to Sunday. This field marks the beginning of the week period. Used for filtering timesheets by week and enforcing the one-timesheet-per-week constraint per employee.

plainFields.name: week_end_date
plainFields.description:
End date of the timesheet week (Sunday).

This field marks the end of the week period. Together with week_start_date, it defines the complete week range for the timesheet. Used for date range queries and timesheet validation.

plainFields.name: approved_at
plainFields.description:
Timestamp when the timesheet was approved.

This field is populated only when status is 'approved'. Records the exact moment of approval for audit trail and reporting. Used to calculate approval turnaround times and generate approval history reports.

plainFields.name: rejected_at
plainFields.description:
Timestamp when the timesheet was rejected.

This field is populated only when the timesheet transitions from 'submitted' to 'rejected'. Records the rejection time for audit purposes. Used in conjunction with rejection_reason to provide complete rejection context.

plainFields.name: rejection_reason
plainFields.description:
Reason provided by the approver when rejecting the timesheet.

This field is required when rejecting a submitted timesheet. The reason is recorded for the employee to review and address issues before resubmission. Used for communication and tracking common rejection patterns.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description:
Timestamp when the timesheet was first created.

Automatically set on timesheet creation. Used for audit trail, sorting timesheets by creation date, and tracking timesheet lifecycle duration.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description:
Timestamp when the timesheet was last modified.

Automatically updated on any timesheet modification. Used for tracking changes, detecting concurrent edits, and sorting by last modification date.

plainFields.name: deleted_at
plainFields.description:
Timestamp when the timesheet was soft deleted.

Nullable field for soft delete support. When set, the timesheet is marked as deleted but preserved in the database. Enables data recovery and maintains referential integrity with related records.

models.name: hrm_time_track_timesheet_timelogs
models.description:
Junction table tracking which timelogs are explicitly included in which timesheets for approval processing.

This table establishes the many-to-many relationship between {@link hrm_time_track_timesheets} and {@link hrm_time_track_timelogs}. Each entry represents an explicit inclusion of a timelog in a timesheet for the weekly approval workflow.

The unique constraint on timesheet_id and timelog_id prevents duplicate associations, ensuring each timelog appears only once per timesheet. This supports the timesheet approval process where employees submit weekly collections of timelogs for manager review.

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: Primary key for the timesheet-timelog association record.

foreignFields.name: hrm_time_track_timesheet_id
foreignFields.description:
Foreign key reference to the parent timesheet that includes this timelog.

This establishes the relationship to {@link hrm_time_track_timesheets}, identifying which weekly timesheet collection contains this timelog entry. The timesheet provides the approval context and week boundaries for the included timelog.

foreignFields.name: hrm_time_track_timelog_id
foreignFields.description:
Foreign key reference to the timelog included in this timesheet.

This establishes the relationship to {@link hrm_time_track_timelogs}, identifying which individual time entry is being submitted for approval as part of the weekly timesheet. The timelog contains the actual work time data.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description:
Timestamp when this timelog was added to the timesheet.

This field tracks when the association was created, providing audit information about when timelogs were included in timesheets for approval processing.

models.name: hrm_time_track_timers
models.description:
Active time tracking sessions for employees with project and optional task association, supporting real-time time recording.

This table stores currently running timer sessions that track work time as it happens. Each employee can have at most one active timer at any time, enforced by the unique constraint on (hrm_time_track_employee_id, is_active) where is_active is true. The timer captures the start timestamp, associated project, optional task, and work description.

When a timer is stopped, it creates a timelog with the calculated duration rounded to the nearest minute and the timer record is removed. When discarded, the timer session ends without creating a timelog. Timers continue running indefinitely if not stopped, with no automatic termination mechanism.

The table enforces data isolation per organization through the employee relationship, ensuring employees can only create timers for projects within their current organization context.

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: Primary Key for the timer session.

foreignFields.name: hrm_time_track_employee_id
foreignFields.description:
Foreign key to the employee who started this timer session.

This establishes the ownership relationship between the employee and their active timer. Each employee can have at most one active timer at any time, enforced by the unique constraint on (hrm_time_track_employee_id, is_active) where is_active is true. The employee must be a member of the organization and assigned to the project referenced in this timer.

foreignFields.name: hrm_time_track_project_id
foreignFields.description:
Foreign key to the project this timer is tracking time against.

Project association is required when starting a timer. The employee must be assigned to this project through hrm_time_track_project_members. This ensures employees can only track time on projects they have access to within their organization.

foreignFields.name: hrm_time_track_task_id
foreignFields.description:
Foreign key to the optional task within the project this timer is tracking.

Task association is optional when starting a timer. If specified, the task must belong to the project referenced in hrm_time_track_project_id. This allows for more granular time tracking at the task level. The employee should be assigned to or have access to this task.

plainFields.name: started_at
plainFields.description:
Timestamp marking when the timer session began.

This field is set when the timer is started and serves as the reference point for calculating elapsed time. The duration is calculated by subtracting started_at from the current time when the timer is stopped. The duration is rounded to the nearest minute when creating the resulting timelog.

plainFields.name: description
plainFields.description:
Optional description of the work being performed during this timer session.

Employees can use this field to note what specific work is being done, providing context for the time being tracked. This description can be edited while the timer is running, allowing corrections and updates to work context without stopping the timer session.

plainFields.name: is_active
plainFields.description:
Flag indicating whether this timer session is currently active.

This field distinguishes between active timers (is_active = true) and inactive timers (is_active = false). The unique constraint on (hrm_time_track_employee_id, is_active) where is_active is true ensures each employee can have at most one active timer at any time. When a timer is stopped or discarded, this field is set to false before the record is eventually removed.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description:
Timestamp when this timer record was created in the database.

This field is automatically set when the timer session is started and provides an audit trail of when the timer was initiated. It should match or be very close to the started_at timestamp.

plainFields.name: updated_at
plainFields.description:
Timestamp when this timer record was last modified.

This field is updated whenever the timer's description, project, or task assignment is edited while the timer is running. It provides visibility into when changes were made to the timer session context.

models.name: hrm_time_track_timesheet_snapshots
models.description:
Immutable audit trail capturing timesheet status changes including submission, approval, and rejection events.

Each snapshot records a point-in-time status change for a timesheet, enabling organizations to review the complete approval history. Snapshots are created automatically when timesheet status transitions occur, providing compliance and audit capabilities.

This table supports the timesheet approval workflow by maintaining a permanent record of all status changes, including who performed each action and when it occurred.

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: Primary Key for timesheet snapshot records.

foreignFields.name: hrm_time_track_timesheet_id
foreignFields.description:
References the timesheet this snapshot captures.

Links to {@link hrm_time_track_timesheets} to identify which timesheet experienced the status change. Multiple snapshots can exist for a single timesheet as it progresses through the approval workflow.

foreignFields.name: hrm_time_track_member_id
foreignFields.description:
References the member who performed the status change action.

Links to {@link hrm_time_track_members} to identify which user submitted, approved, or rejected the timesheet. This provides accountability for all timesheet status transitions.

plainFields.name: status
plainFields.description:
The timesheet status captured at the time of this snapshot.

Records the status value (draft, submitted, approved, or rejected) that the timesheet had when this snapshot was created. This denormalized field enables efficient querying of status history without joining to the timesheet table.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description:
Timestamp when this snapshot was created.

Records the exact moment the status change occurred, providing precise timing information for audit purposes and compliance reporting.

models.name: hrm_time_track_timer_snapshots
models.description:
Historical record of timer sessions capturing start, stop, discard, and edit events for compliance and reporting.

This snapshot table maintains an immutable audit trail of all timer lifecycle events. Each timer event creates a snapshot record that captures the timer state at that moment, ensuring compliance requirements are met and providing complete visibility into time tracking activities.

Snapshots are created for the following events:
- Start: When a timer begins tracking time
- Stop: When a timer completes and records duration
- Discard: When a timer is cancelled without recording time
- Edit: When timer attributes are modified after creation

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: Primary Key for timer snapshot records.

foreignFields.name: hrm_time_track_timer_id
foreignFields.description:
Foreign key reference to the parent timer entity.

This establishes the relationship between the snapshot and the timer it represents. Multiple snapshots can exist for a single timer as it progresses through its lifecycle.

foreignFields.name: hrm_time_track_employee_id
foreignFields.description:
Foreign key reference to the employee who owns the timer.

This denormalized field captures the employee association at the time of the snapshot event, ensuring the audit trail remains complete even if employee records are updated or deleted.

foreignFields.name: hrm_time_track_project_id
foreignFields.description:
Foreign key reference to the project the timer is associated with.

This denormalized field captures the project association at the time of the snapshot event, ensuring accurate project time tracking records.

foreignFields.name: hrm_time_track_task_id
foreignFields.description:
Foreign key reference to the optional task the timer is associated with.

This denormalized field captures the task association at the time of the snapshot event. Timers can be associated with projects only (without specific tasks), making this field nullable.

foreignFields.name: created_by
foreignFields.description:
Foreign key reference to the member who created this snapshot.

This captures which user performed the action that triggered the snapshot event, providing accountability for timer operations.

plainFields.name: event_type
plainFields.description:
Type of timer event that triggered this snapshot.

Allowed values:
- 'start': Timer began tracking time
- 'stop': Timer completed and recorded duration
- 'discard': Timer was cancelled without recording time
- 'edit': Timer attributes were modified after creation

plainFields.name: duration_seconds
plainFields.description:
Duration in seconds recorded at the time of this snapshot event.

For 'start' events, this value is 0. For 'stop' events, this contains the total tracked duration. For 'discard' events, this may contain partial duration or 0. For 'edit' events, this reflects the modified duration.

plainFields.name: started_at
plainFields.description:
Timestamp when the timer was originally started.

This field captures the start time of the timer session and remains constant across all snapshots for the same timer, even if the timer is edited.

plainFields.name: stopped_at
plainFields.description:
Timestamp when the timer was stopped.

This field is populated for 'stop' and 'edit' events when the timer has been completed. For 'start' events and active timers, this field is null.

plainFields.name: note
plainFields.description:
Optional note or description attached to the timer.

This field captures any additional context or comments provided by the employee about the time being tracked. The note is denormalized from the parent timer to preserve the exact text at the time of the snapshot.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description:
Timestamp when this snapshot record was created.

This field indicates when the timer event occurred and the snapshot was recorded. It serves as the chronological marker for the audit trail.

models.name: hrm_time_track_activity_logs
models.description:
Organization-wide audit trail capturing all significant actions including employee lifecycle events, contract changes, project lifecycle events, task status changes, timesheet submissions, and role assignments.

This table provides an immutable record of all important system events for compliance, security auditing, and transparency. Each activity log entry is append-only and cannot be modified or deleted once created.

Activity types include employee creation/deactivation, contract modifications, project creation/completion, task status transitions, timesheet submissions/approvals, and role assignments. The metadata field stores action-specific details in a normalized key-value structure.

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: Primary Key for activity log entry.

foreignFields.name: hrm_time_track_organization_id
foreignFields.description:
Organization that owns this activity log entry.

All activity logs are scoped to a specific organization for multi-tenancy isolation. Users can only view activity logs from organizations they belong to.

foreignFields.name: hrm_time_track_member_id
foreignFields.description:
User who performed the action recorded in this activity log.

This establishes accountability by tracking which authenticated user triggered the event.

foreignFields.name: hrm_time_track_employee_id
foreignFields.description:
Employee entity affected by this activity, if applicable.

Used for employee lifecycle events such as creation, deactivation, department changes, or role assignments.

foreignFields.name: hrm_time_track_project_id
foreignFields.description:
Project entity affected by this activity, if applicable.

Used for project lifecycle events such as creation, status changes, or archival.

foreignFields.name: hrm_time_track_task_id
foreignFields.description:
Task entity affected by this activity, if applicable.

Used for task status changes, assignment modifications, or due date updates.

foreignFields.name: hrm_time_track_timesheet_id
foreignFields.description:
Timesheet entity affected by this activity, if applicable.

Used for timesheet submission, approval, or rejection events.

foreignFields.name: hrm_time_track_role_id
foreignFields.description:
Role entity affected by this activity, if applicable.

Used for role creation, modification, or deletion events.

foreignFields.name: hrm_time_track_employee_contract_id
foreignFields.description:
Employee contract entity affected by this activity, if applicable.

Used for contract creation, modification, or termination events.

foreignFields.name: hrm_time_track_department_id
foreignFields.description:
Department entity affected by this activity, if applicable.

Used for department creation, modification, or deletion events.

plainFields.name: activity_type
plainFields.description:
Category of the activity being logged.

Standard types include: employee_created, employee_deactivated, contract_created, contract_modified, project_created, project_archived, task_status_changed, timesheet_submitted, timesheet_approved, timesheet_rejected, role_assigned, role_created, department_created, etc.

plainFields.name: description
plainFields.description:
Human-readable description of the activity.

Provides context about what happened, who was involved, and any relevant details for audit purposes.

plainFields.name: metadata
plainFields.description:
Structured data containing action-specific details.

Stores key-value pairs or JSON-like data for complex activity details that don't fit standard fields. This allows flexible storage of event-specific information while maintaining the core schema.

plainFields.name: ip_address
plainFields.description:
IP address of the user who performed the action.

Used for security auditing and geolocation tracking of activity sources.

plainFields.name: user_agent
plainFields.description:
Browser or client user agent string of the user who performed the action.

Provides technical context about the client environment used to trigger the activity.

plainFields.name: created_at
plainFields.description:
Timestamp when the activity occurred.

This is the actual time of the event, not when the record was inserted. Used for chronological ordering and time-range queries.

models.name: hrm_time_track_task_histories
models.description:
Immutable audit trail of task status changes.

Records every status transition for tasks, capturing the previous status, new status, timestamp of change, and the member who performed the change. This table provides a complete audit trail for compliance and tracking task progression.

Each history entry is append-only and cannot be modified or deleted after creation, ensuring an accurate record of all task status changes.

primaryField.name: id
primaryField.description: Primary Key for task history record.

foreignFields.name: hrm_time_track_task_id
foreignFields.description:
Reference to the task whose status changed.

Links to {@link hrm_time_track_tasks} to identify which task this history entry belongs to. Multiple history entries can exist for a single task as it progresses through different statuses.

foreignFields.name: hrm_time_track_member_id
foreignFields.description:
Reference to the member who made the status change.

Links to {@link hrm_time_track_members} to identify which user performed the status transition. This enables accountability and audit tracking of who changed task statuses.

plainFields.name: previous_status
plainFields.description:
The task status before the change occurred.

Captures the previous state to enable tracking of status transitions over time. This field is essential for understanding the progression of tasks through their lifecycle.

plainFields.name: new_status
plainFields.description:
The new task status after the change.

Timestamp when the status change occurred.
